fact: Released deliberately in Australia in 1950, and the best-documented case of a pathogen and its host evolving against each other.

name: Batrachochytrium
fact: A fungus that has driven more vertebrate species to extinction than any other single pathogen known.

name: White-Nose Fungus
fact: A cold-loving fungus that grows on hibernating bats at temperatures where nothing can fight it.

name: Varroa Mite
fact: A mite the size of a dinner plate on a person, feeding on the bee's fat body and carrying viruses in.

name: Paenibacillus Larvae
fact: American foulbrood: the reason beekeepers burn hives rather than treat them.

name: Nosema
fact: A microsporidian — a fungus that has thrown away its own mitochondria and steals ATP from its host.

name: Dirofilaria Immitis
fact: Heartworm: a nematode up to thirty centimetres long living in the pulmonary artery.

name: Sarcoptes Scabiei
fact: A mite that tunnels in the skin, and the same species causes scabies in people and mange in animals.

name: Theileria
fact: The only eukaryotic parasite known to transform a host cell into something like a cancer.

name: Babesia
fact: A tick-borne parasite of red blood cells, and the cause of Texas cattle fever.

name: Mite
fact: Eight legs, usually under a millimetre, and there are more of them in a handful of soil than almost anything else.

name: Midge
fact: A biting fly small enough to pass through mosquito netting, and it carries bluetongue.

name: Variola
fact: Smallpox: the only human disease ever eradicated, and it had no animal reservoir to hide in.

name: SARS-CoV-2
fact: A coronavirus that spreads before people feel ill, which is what made it uncontainable.

name: Coronavirus
fact: Named for the crown of spikes around it, and it carries the largest genome of any RNA virus.

name: Ebola Virus
fact: A filovirus that spreads only by contact with the very ill or the newly dead.

name: Marburg Virus
fact: The first filovirus ever identified, and it was found in a European laboratory in 1967.

name: Lassa Virus
fact: Carried by one species of rat that lives in houses across West Africa, and shed in its urine.

name: Nipah Virus
fact: It reached people through pigs the first time, and through date palm sap the second.

name: Hantavirus
fact: Breathed in from dried rodent urine and droppings, and person-to-person spread is essentially absent.

name: Dengue Virus
fact: Four types, and surviving one makes the next one worse rather than better.

name: Zika Virus
fact: Known since 1947 and considered trivial until 2015, when it was found to cross the placenta.

name: Chikungunya Virus
fact: The name means 'that which bends up', for the posture of someone with the joint pain.

name: Hepatitis B
fact: A DNA virus that copies itself through an RNA intermediate, like a retrovirus running backwards.

name: Hepatitis C
fact: Found in 1989 by cloning the genome of something nobody had ever seen, and curable since 2014.

name: Herpes Simplex
fact: It retreats into a nerve cell body and waits there for the rest of your life.

name: Varicella Zoster
fact: One virus, two diseases, decades apart — and the second one is the first one coming back.

name: Chickenpox
fact: Not related to smallpox at all, despite two centuries of the two being confused.

name: Rotavirus
fact: Before the vaccine it killed around half a million children a year, and it infects essentially everyone.

name: Mycobacterium Leprae
fact: It has lost about a third of its own genes and cannot be grown in any culture medium.

name: Borrelia Burgdorferi
fact: Lyme disease, and its genome is split across a chromosome and more than twenty plasmids.

name: Shigella
fact: Genetically it is Escherichia coli, and it is kept as a separate genus for historical reasons only.

name: Candida Albicans
fact: A yeast most people carry harmlessly, which turns invasive by changing its shape.

name: Aspergillus Fumigatus
fact: Everyone breathes in hundreds of its spores a day, and almost nobody is harmed.

name: Cryptococcus Neoformans
fact: A yeast with a thick sugar capsule, found in pigeon droppings and in old tree hollows.

name: Schistosoma Mansoni
fact: A fluke whose male and female live permanently paired, the female held in a groove along his body.

name: Necator Americanus
fact: Hookworm: it enters through the sole of a bare foot and ends up in the small intestine.

name: Canine Distemper Virus
fact: A close relative of measles and rinderpest, and it does not stay in dogs.

name: Feline Leukaemia Virus
fact: A retrovirus that inserts itself into the cat's own chromosomes, and sometimes lands in the wrong place.

name: Pain
fact: A signal, not a substance — and the only symptom that is entirely private to the person having it.

name: Anaemia
fact: Not too little blood, but too little of the thing in it that carries oxygen.

name: Thyroid
fact: A butterfly-shaped gland that sets the speed at which the whole body runs.

name: Goitre
fact: The gland swelling because it is being told to work harder and lacks the one ingredient it needs.

name: Heart Attack
fact: The heart muscle starving because one of the vessels feeding it has closed.

name: Heart Failure
fact: Not the heart stopping, but the heart no longer keeping up with what is asked of it.

name: Stroke
fact: Brain tissue dying because its blood supply stopped, or because a vessel burst into it.

name: Asthma
fact: The airway narrowing from the inside, and it is reversible, which is what separates it from everything else.

name: Arthritis
fact: Two quite different diseases share the name, and telling them apart decides everything.

name: Osteoporosis
fact: Bone is being replaced all your life, and this is what happens when the replacing falls behind.

name: Cataract
fact: The lens clouding because its proteins, which are never replaced, have clumped.

name: Ulcer
fact: For a century the cause was thought to be stress and spice. It is mostly a bacterium.

name: Haemophilia
fact: One missing clotting protein, and the gene for it sits on the X chromosome.

name: Gout
fact: Uric acid crystallising in a joint, and it picks the coldest one — usually the big toe.

name: Lead Poisoning
fact: Lead has no biological role at all, and the body mistakes it for calcium.

name: Carbon Monoxide Poisoning
fact: It binds the same site as oxygen, about two hundred times more tightly, and it has no smell.

name: Dehydration
fact: Losing water is survivable for a while. Losing water and salt together is what kills.

name: Hypothermia
fact: The body has a very narrow range it works in, and two degrees below it the shivering stops.

name: Altitude Sickness
fact: The air is the same mixture all the way up. There is simply less of it pressing down.

name: Pellagra
fact: The four Ds — dermatitis, diarrhoea, dementia, death — from a diet built on maize.

name: Beriberi
fact: It arrived with the machine that polished rice, and nobody connected the two for decades.

name: Night Blindness
fact: The first thing to fail when vitamin A runs short, because the eye spends it fastest.

name: Kwashiorkor
fact: A swollen belly on a starving child, and the swelling is why it was misread for so long.

name: Childbirth
fact: The only routine event in medicine where two patients share one body and their interests can differ.

name: Labour
fact: Contractions that build on themselves, because the thing that causes them is released by them.

name: Vitamin B1
fact: Thiamine: the first vitamin to be identified, and the reason the word exists at all.

name: Bran
fact: The outer layer milled off to make white flour, and it carries most of what was worth eating.

name: Hypothyroidism
fact: The gland running slow, and everything downstream of it running slow too.

name: Bradycardia
fact: A heart beating too slowly to keep the brain supplied.

name: Stator
fact: The half that stays still, and in a generator it is usually where the useful current is made.

name: Anode
fact: The electrode where oxidation happens — and which end that is depends on which way the current is going.

name: Cathode
fact: The electrode where reduction happens, and the one metal is deposited onto.

name: Electrode
fact: The point where a circuit stops being wire and starts being chemistry.

name: Electrolyte
fact: A liquid that carries ions but not electrons, which is exactly what a battery needs between its plates.

name: Terminal
fact: Where the device stops and your wiring starts, and most electrical faults are here.

name: Casing
fact: The part whose whole job is that nothing inside it is your problem.

name: Commutator
fact: A rotary switch that reverses the connection twice per turn, so the torque never changes sign.

name: Armature
fact: The winding that moves through the field — or the field that moves past the winding.

name: Insulator
fact: Not the absence of conduction but the deliberate maintenance of it, over decades, in weather.

name: Bushing
fact: The way a live conductor gets through an earthed metal wall without arcing to it.

name: Loudspeaker
fact: A coil in a magnetic field, glued to a cone, and it is a microphone run backwards.

name: Warp
fact: The threads that run the length of the cloth, held under tension for the whole weaving.

name: Weft
fact: The thread that crosses, and the only one that actually has to travel.

name: Heddle
fact: A loop that one warp thread passes through, so that lifting it lifts that thread and no other.

name: Shed
fact: The triangular gap opened between raised and lowered warp threads, and it exists for about a second.

name: Shuttle
fact: A boat-shaped case carrying the weft, thrown from one side to the other.

name: Bobbin
fact: A spool sized to fit inside whatever has to carry it.

name: Cam
fact: A shaped disc that turns rotation into a pushing that follows whatever profile you cut.

name: Feed Dog
fact: The toothed bar under the needle plate that moves the cloth along, a stitch at a time.

name: Tension Disc
fact: Two plates squeezed by a spring, with the thread running between them.

name: Pivot
fact: The point a thing turns on, and in an instrument it is sharpened almost to nothing.

name: Jewel
fact: A synthetic sapphire with a hole in it, used as a bearing because it will not wear.

name: Gimbal
fact: Rings pivoted at right angles, so that whatever they carry stays level while the ship rolls.

name: Ring
fact: A closed curve of material, and the shape that carries a pull evenly all the way round.

name: Vacuum
fact: Not nothing — just less than there was, and the difference is what does the work.

name: Cistern
fact: A reservoir that holds a head of water so the supply is steady rather than intermittent.

name: Mouldboard
fact: The curved plate that lifts the cut slice and turns it over, and the curve is the whole invention.

name: Ploughshare
fact: The wedge that cuts the furrow horizontally, and the part that wears out first.

name: Wedge
fact: One of the six simple machines, and the only one you hit.

name: Nozzle
fact: A narrowing that trades pressure for speed, and past a certain point it must widen again.

name: Governor
fact: Two weights that fly outward as the engine speeds up, and close the steam as they do.

name: Flyweight
fact: A weight on an arm, thrown outward by rotation, and its position reports the speed.

name: Rind
fact: The skin a cheese grows, and it is not a wrapper — it is the outside of the cheese behaving differently.

name: Filter
fact: A barrier chosen so that what you want goes through and what you do not stays behind.

name: Kernel
fact: The part of an operating system that is always resident, and the only part allowed to touch the hardware.

name: Scheduler
fact: Decides which program runs next, and it does this thousands of times a second.

name: Device Driver
fact: The translation between what the operating system asks for and what one particular piece of hardware wants.

name: Interrupt
fact: A device saying 'now' loudly enough that the processor stops what it was doing.

name: Process
fact: A running program, together with everything it thinks is its own.

name: Signature
fact: A single sheet folded down to make several leaves, and books are built from these rather than from pages.

name: Horizon
fact: The line where you stop being able to see, and its distance tells you how high you are.

name: Morse Code
fact: The commonest letters get the shortest signals, which is why E is one dot.

name: Exchange
fact: Wiring every telephone to every other needs a wire for each pair. An exchange needs one wire each.

name: Valley
fact: The river makes it. The mountains are just what is left standing either side.

name: Gorge
fact: A valley cut faster than its walls can fall in, which is what makes it narrow.

name: Cliff
fact: Not carved so much as continually broken off at the bottom.

name: Scree
fact: The pile of broken rock at the foot of a slope, and it always settles at about the same angle.

name: Snowline
fact: The height above which snow lasts the summer, and it is a line you can see.

name: Treeline
fact: The height above which trees stop, and it is temperature rather than cold that sets it.

name: Erosion
fact: The whole landscape is temporary, and this is the rate.

name: Crater
fact: Always round, whatever angle the thing arrived at, because it is an explosion and not a dent.

name: Hot Spring
fact: Rain that fell years ago, went down far enough to be heated, and found a way back up.

name: Sunset
fact: The blue light has been scattered out of the beam before it reaches you, and only the red is left.

name: Hearth
fact: A fire given a permanent place, and that is the moment a shelter becomes a house.

name: Molasses
fact: What is left after the sugar has been crystallised out, and it holds most of what was not sugar.

name: Rum
fact: Distilled from the waste of sugar making, which is why it belongs to the Caribbean and not to a grain country.

name: Cologne
fact: Named after the city, and it is defined by being weak — two to five per cent oil, where perfume is twenty.

name: Currency
fact: Money that a particular authority says is money, and its value rests on that saying.

name: Pound Sterling
fact: The oldest currency still in use, and the name was once literally a pound of silver.

name: Dollar
fact: The name comes from a Bohemian valley, and it is now the currency of about twenty countries.

name: Poodle
fact: A working water dog, and the haircut everyone laughs at was cut for a reason.

name: Labradoodle
fact: Bred in Australia in 1989 to be a guide dog someone with an allergy could keep.

name: Cassowary
fact: The most dangerous bird alive, and the claw that does it is on the inner toe.

name: Ratite
fact: Flightless birds with no keel on the breastbone, and they did not lose flight once.

name: Mustelid
fact: Long body, short legs, and a scent gland that is the family signature.

name: Weasel
fact: The smallest carnivore there is, and small enough to follow a vole underground.

name: Badger
fact: A mustelid that went the other way: heavy, powerful, and built to dig rather than to follow.

name: System
fact: Parts whose behaviour together is not in any of them separately.

name: Cycle
fact: A process whose end is its own beginning, which is why it can run forever on nothing but energy passing through.

name: Theory
fact: In science it is the strongest thing there is, and in ordinary speech it means a guess. That gap causes most public arguments about science.

name: Evidence
fact: An observation only becomes evidence in relation to a claim — the same fact can support one and refute another.

name: Observation
fact: Looking at something without changing it, which is harder than it sounds and sometimes impossible.

name: Measurement
fact: Comparing a thing to an agreed unit, and the agreement is the hard part.

name: Standard
fact: Something everyone agrees to do the same way, and its whole value is that nobody defects.

name: Agreement
fact: Two parties choosing to be predictable to each other, which is what makes anything past barter possible.

name: Trust
fact: Acting on an expectation you cannot verify, and it is cheaper than verifying.

name: Selection
fact: Not a force and not a chooser. Just the arithmetic of what leaves more descendants.

name: Variation
fact: The differences within a species, and without it nothing can evolve at all.

name: Population
fact: The unit evolution actually acts on. An individual cannot evolve.

name: Bond
fact: Atoms sharing or handing over electrons, and everything chemistry does is this.

name: Gland
fact: An organ whose whole job is to make something and release it.

name: Lobe
fact: A part of an organ marked off by a groove, and in the brain the grooves came before the names.

name: Fissure
fact: A deep groove, and in a brain it is what lets a large sheet fit in a small box.

name: Fold
fact: Doubling something over, which multiplies its area in a given space and its stiffness along the crease.

name: Structure
fact: The arrangement that decides what a thing can carry, and it usually matters more than what it is made of.

name: Form
fact: What a thing is, as distinct from what it is made of — the oldest distinction in philosophy and still the useful one.

name: Load
fact: What a structure has to carry, and the temporary ones usually decide the design.

name: Code
fact: An agreed mapping between symbols and meanings, and it does not have to be secret.

name: Symbol
fact: A mark that stands for something by agreement rather than by resemblance.

name: Meaning
fact: What a sign points to, and it lives in the reader rather than in the mark.

name: Mark
fact: The oldest technology for making something outlast the moment it was made in.

name: Machine
fact: Something that changes a force's size or direction, and there are only six of them underneath.

name: Motor
fact: A generator run backwards, and the same machine will do either.

name: Giant
fact: What a star becomes when it runs out of hydrogen in its core, and it gets bigger by cooling.

name: Dwarf
fact: What is left when a star has nothing to burn and nothing holding it up but the electrons themselves.

name: Helix
fact: A circle that is also travelling, and the shape a chain takes when every link turns by the same angle.

name: Axis
fact: The line a thing turns about, and it is the one part that does not move.

name: Rotation
fact: Turning about a line rather than moving along one, and it conserves its own quantity.

name: Zone
fact: A band where conditions are similar enough that the same things live or happen throughout it.

name: Region
fact: An area treated as one thing, and what makes it one is a decision.

name: Boundary
fact: Where one thing stops being itself, and it is nearly always a gradient someone has drawn a line across.

name: Edge
fact: Where a surface ends, and in ecology it is where most of the life is.

name: Perception
fact: Not a recording of the world but the brain's best guess at what would explain the signals.

name: Consciousness
fact: The only thing anyone has direct evidence of, and the only thing nobody can demonstrate to anyone else.

name: Attention
fact: Not looking harder — deciding what to leave out.

name: Emotion
fact: The body changes first and the feeling names it afterwards, which is the opposite of how it seems.

name: Fear
fact: It takes a fast road that reaches the body before you know what you saw.

name: Anger
fact: The one negative emotion that makes people approach rather than withdraw.

name: Happiness
fact: Wanting and liking are different systems, and only one of them is happiness.

name: Love
fact: Three separate systems that evolved for different jobs and do not have to point at the same person.

name: Attachment
fact: An infant's tie to whoever comes when it cries, formed in the first year and audible in adults decades later.

name: Grief
fact: The cost of attachment, and it arrives in the shape of the thing that is gone.

name: Dream
fact: The brain runs while the body is switched off at the spine, which is why you can fly and not fall out of bed.

name: Sleep
fact: Every animal with a nervous system does it, and it costs so much that it must be paying for something.

name: Thought
fact: Much of it is not in words, which is why the right word is so hard to find.

name: Reason
fact: It arrives at conclusions the arguer already held far more often than it arrives anywhere new.

name: Learning
fact: The synapse changes, and the change is the memory.

name: Repetition
fact: Spacing it out beats massing it together, and this has been known and ignored since 1885.

name: Intelligence
fact: Whatever it is, it is not one thing, and the argument about that is the whole history of the subject.

name: Problem
fact: A gap between where you are and where you want to be, plus not knowing the way.

name: Want
fact: Wanting is not the same system as liking, and it is the one that keeps you going.

name: Need
fact: What an organism must have or fail, which is a much shorter list than what it wants.

name: Belief
fact: Holding something to be so, and it is what you act on rather than what you say.

name: Knowledge
fact: Justified true belief — and Gettier showed in three pages in 1963 that this is not enough.

name: Philosophy
fact: The discipline that keeps losing its subjects, and that is what it is for.

name: Question
fact: A shape in the language for the gap where an answer would go.

name: Ethics
fact: The question of what to do, which cannot be answered by finding out what is the case.

name: Art
fact: A made thing whose purpose is to be attended to, and every attempt to define it more tightly has failed.

name: Colour
fact: Not a property of things. A property of the conversation between a surface, a light and three kinds of cell.

name: Story
fact: Events put in an order that implies why, which is not the order they happened in.

name: Myth
fact: A story a culture treats as explaining why things are as they are, rather than as something that once happened.

name: Ritual
fact: Actions whose form matters more than their effect, done the same way because that is the way.

name: Festival
fact: A date the whole community stops on, and almost all of them sit on the farming year.

name: Dance
fact: Movement made to be watched and to be synchronised with, and the synchronising is the older function.

name: Song
fact: Words and pitch together, and it is easier to remember than either alone.

name: Poetry
fact: Language arranged so the form carries meaning too, and the constraint is what does the work.

name: Instrument
fact: Something that turns a small motion into a loud sound, which is a problem of matching rather than of amplifying.

name: Resonator
fact: A body that answers at one pitch and ignores the rest.

name: Painting
fact: Pigment held in a binder on a surface, and the binder decides almost everything about it.

name: Sculpture
fact: Carving is subtractive and cannot be undone, which is why so much of it was worked out in clay first.

name: Architecture
fact: Building with the load in mind, and for most of history the mathematics followed the buildings rather than led them.

name: Tradition
fact: Information passed by copying rather than by inheritance, which lets it change far faster than genes.

name: Generation
fact: The interval between a parent and a child, and it sets the clock for everything inherited.

name: Play
fact: Practising things that matter, at a time when getting them wrong is cheap.

name: Sport
fact: A contest with agreed constraints, and the constraints are what make it worth watching.

name: Rule
fact: A constraint accepted in advance, which is what makes the outcome mean something.

name: Humour
fact: Something is set up to go one way and goes another, safely, and the laugh is the release.

name: Surprise
fact: The size of the gap between what was predicted and what arrived, and the brain is built to measure it.

name: Expectation
fact: The brain runs slightly ahead of the world, and what you perceive is mostly the prediction.

name: Pattern
fact: A regularity that lets you say what comes next, which is the only reason it is worth finding.

name: Fashion
fact: Change for its own sake, and the speed of the change is the signal rather than the clothes.

name: Ratio
fact: One quantity against another, and it is the first thing that stops depending on the units.

name: Division
fact: Sharing out, and the one arithmetic operation with a forbidden case.

name: Part
fact: Something considered separately from what it belongs to, and the separating is a decision.

name: Whole
fact: What the parts add up to, and it usually has properties none of them has.

name: Fraction
fact: A number between the whole ones, and admitting they exist took a very long time.

name: Limit
fact: What a thing gets arbitrarily close to without ever having to arrive.

name: Infinity
fact: Not one size. Cantor showed there are infinitely many infinities, and some are strictly bigger.

name: Change
fact: The only thing measurable without a second object to compare against.

name: Difference
fact: The first thing any measurement produces, and often the only thing that is real.

name: Calculus
fact: The mathematics of things that are changing, invented twice at once and argued over for a century.

name: Axiom
fact: A starting point assumed rather than shown, because something has to be.

name: Proof
fact: A chain from things agreed to a thing not yet agreed, where every link can be checked on its own.

name: Theorem
fact: A statement shown to follow, and it stays shown.

name: Contradiction
fact: A statement and its denial both held, and it is fatal because everything follows from it.

name: Paradox
fact: An argument that looks sound and reaches something that cannot be, which means an assumption is wrong.

name: Equation
fact: A claim that two descriptions pick out the same thing, which is why it can be rearranged.

name: Function
fact: A rule giving exactly one output for each input, and the 'exactly one' is the whole definition.

name: Event
fact: Something happening at a place and a time, which is the smallest thing physics will discuss.

name: Outcome
fact: One of the ways a thing could have turned out, and listing them properly is most of the work.

name: Chance
fact: Either the world is not determined, or we do not know enough. The mathematics is the same either way.

name: Probability
fact: It began as a way of splitting the stake in an interrupted gambling game.

name: Sample
fact: A part chosen to stand for the whole, and how it was chosen matters more than how big it is.

name: Statistics
fact: Reasoning from a part to the whole, which is always a bet.

name: Average
fact: A single number standing for many, and it can describe a set containing nothing like it.

name: Symmetry
fact: A change that makes no difference, and every conservation law is one.

name: Pi
fact: The same number for every circle there has ever been, and it never ends or repeats.

name: Season
fact: Caused by the tilt, not the distance. Earth is closest to the Sun in January.

name: Era
fact: A stretch of time named after the fact, by people deciding where the joins were.

name: Past
fact: Fixed, and known only through what happened to survive.

name: Future
fact: Not yet fixed, and the only part of time anything can be done about.

name: Prehistory
fact: Everything before writing, which is over ninety-five per cent of it.

name: Bronze Age
fact: Named for an alloy whose two metals are almost never found in the same place.

name: Iron Age
fact: Iron is a worse metal than bronze until you can work it, and far commoner once you can.

name: Antiquity
fact: The period with written records and no continuous institutions reaching us, which is why it needed rediscovering.

name: Middle Ages
fact: Named by people who thought of it as the gap between two better times, which is a judgement rather than a period.

name: Renaissance
fact: A rediscovery, and the press is why this one did not fade like the earlier ones.

name: Modernity
fact: The period that thinks of itself as new, which is itself the novelty.

name: Archaeology
fact: Reading the ground, in which depth is time and disturbance is the enemy.

name: Industry
fact: Making things by machine rather than by hand, and the change was in the power rather than the tools.

name: Fuel
fact: Anything holding chemical energy loosely enough to be released on purpose.

name: Natural Gas
fact: Mostly methane, and for a century it was burnt off at the wellhead as a nuisance.

name: Refinery
fact: One input and a dozen products, separated by nothing more than boiling point.

name: Mining
fact: Taking rock out of the ground for the small part of it that is wanted.

name: Solar Power
fact: A photon knocks an electron loose and the junction decides which way it goes.

name: Sunlight
fact: Eight minutes old when it arrives, and the energy in it left the core about a hundred thousand years before that.

name: Wind Power
fact: No turbine can take more than about 59% of the wind's energy, and that is a theorem.

name: Hydroelectricity
fact: The only large-scale way of storing grid electricity that anyone actually uses.

name: Dam
fact: It holds back water with its own weight, and the pressure it must resist depends on depth rather than on how much is behind it.

name: Nuclear Power
fact: The energy comes from mass that is simply gone, and the amount is set by the most famous equation there is.

name: Fission
fact: A nucleus split by being hit, and it throws out more of what hit it — which is the chain.

name: Waste
fact: A category rather than a substance: it is whatever the process was not for.

name: Recycling
fact: Some materials come back as themselves and some come back worse, and the difference is not about effort.

name: Pollution
fact: The dose and the place, not the substance. Everything is a pollutant somewhere.

name: Tribe
fact: The largest group in which everyone still knows everyone, and that ceiling is roughly 150 people.

name: Justice
fact: Treating like cases alike, which sounds empty until you try to say which cases are alike.

name: Slavery
fact: Owning a person as property, and almost every society practised it until very recently.

name: Class
fact: A division that survives the individuals in it, which is what makes it a class rather than a rank.

name: Peace
fact: Not the absence of war but the presence of something that settles disputes instead.

name: Skeleton
fact: Living tissue with its own blood supply, being rebuilt continuously, and about a fifth of it is replaced each year.

name: Intestine
fact: Seven metres of it, folded into an area of about thirty square metres, which is why it fits.

name: Hormone
fact: A message sent to the whole body, and only the cells with the receptor hear it.

name: Circulation
fact: Harvey worked it out by arithmetic: the heart pumps more blood in an hour than the body contains.

name: Breathing
fact: Driven by carbon dioxide rather than by oxygen, which is why you cannot hold your breath to harm.

name: Birth
fact: The moment the lungs take over from the placenta, and the circulation rearranges itself in seconds.

name: Death
fact: Not one event. Different tissues stop at different times, and where the line is drawn has changed with what medicine can do.

name: Ageing
fact: A cell can divide only about fifty times, and the counter is on the end of the chromosome.

name: Genetics
fact: Mendel's paper sat unread for 34 years, and the mechanism he inferred was found long after he died.

name: Respiration
fact: The same reaction as burning, run in about thirty small steps so the energy comes out in usable pieces.

name: Reproduction
fact: Sex costs half your genes in every offspring, and almost everything complex does it anyway.

name: Predation
fact: It shapes both sides, and the prey is usually running for its life while the predator is running for its dinner.

name: Decomposition
fact: Without it every atom life ever used would still be locked in a corpse.

name: Space
fact: Not a container things sit in. It is a relation between things, and it can stretch.

name: Spacetime
fact: One thing, not two, and different observers slice it differently.

name: Velocity
fact: Speed with a direction, and it only exists relative to something else.

name: Pressure
fact: Force spread over area, which is why a drawing pin works and a bed of nails does not hurt.

name: Heat
fact: Energy in transit because of a temperature difference. A thing does not contain heat.

name: Thermodynamics
fact: Four laws, and the second one is the reason anything happens in a direction.

name: Relativity
fact: It starts from one stubborn fact: everyone measures light at the same speed, however they are moving.

name: Quantum Mechanics
fact: It predicts what fraction of many identical experiments give each result, and refuses to say more.

name: Uncertainty Principle
fact: Not a limit on instruments. A particle does not have a precise position and momentum at once.

name: Rock
fact: An aggregate of minerals, and there are only three ways to make one.

name: Igneous Rock
fact: The crystal size tells you how fast it cooled, and nothing else needs to be known.

name: Sedimentary Rock
fact: The only rock that keeps a record, because it is the only one made without destroying what came before.

name: Metamorphic Rock
fact: Changed by heat and pressure without ever melting, which is the whole definition.

name: Sediment
fact: Sorted by the water that carried it, so grain size records how fast the current was.

name: Silt
fact: Between sand and clay, and it is what makes a floodplain worth farming.

name: Weathering
fact: Breaking rock where it stands, which is different from carrying it away.

name: Reduction
fact: Gaining electrons, and it cannot happen without something else losing them.

name: Solvent
fact: Like dissolves like, and that one rule decides most of what mixes with what.

name: Valence
fact: How many bonds an atom makes, and it is set by how far its outer shell is from full.

name: Organic Chemistry
fact: It was named for the belief that these compounds needed a living thing to make them, which was disproved in 1828.

name: Isomer
fact: The same atoms in the same numbers, arranged differently, and behaving nothing alike.

name: Boiling
fact: It happens when the vapour pressure inside equals the pressure outside, which is why altitude changes the number.

name: Plain
fact: Flat because something levelled it, and usually that something was water.

name: Forest
fact: It makes its own rain, and past a certain size cutting it stops that.

name: Grassland
fact: Kept treeless by fire and grazing, not by climate. Most of it could be forest.

name: Wetland
fact: Waterlogged ground, and the waterlogging is what makes it store carbon instead of releasing it.

name: Coast
fact: The only landscape rebuilt twice a day, and it is a system rather than a line.

name: Prairie
fact: Two metres of the best soil on Earth, made by grass roots dying and being replaced for ten thousand years.

name: Lake
fact: Geologically temporary. Every one of them is filling in, and most last only thousands of years.

name: Groundwater
fact: There is about a hundred times more fresh water below ground than in all the rivers and lakes together.

name: Weather
fact: The atmosphere redistributing heat from the equator to the poles, and everything else is detail.

name: Climate
fact: Weather is what happens; climate is the distribution it is drawn from.

name: Drought
fact: Defined against expectation, so a wet country can have one on rainfall a dry one would call normal.

name: Greenhouse Effect
fact: Without it the Earth would average about minus eighteen degrees. The question has never been whether it exists.

name: Smelting
fact: Not melting. It is a chemical reaction that takes the oxygen off the metal.

name: Casting
fact: Every casting shrinks as it cools, so the pattern must be made larger than the thing wanted.

name: Forging
fact: It does not just shape the metal, it aligns the grain, which is why a forged part is stronger than a machined one.

name: Welding
fact: Making two pieces into one piece, which is different from sticking them together.

name: Weaving
fact: Two sets of thread at right angles, and the cloth's whole behaviour comes from the angle you pull it at.

name: Dyeing
fact: Most dyes will not stay on the fibre without a mordant, which is a metal salt that binds to both.

name: Tanning
fact: Skin rots and leather does not, because the tannin cross-links the collagen so bacteria cannot break it.

name: Food
fact: The only thing an animal must take from outside to rebuild itself with, and it is both fuel and parts.

name: Cooking
fact: It externalises digestion, and it may be why the human gut is short and the brain is large.

name: Baking
fact: Dry heat from all sides, and the crust forms first and then holds the shape.

name: Roasting
fact: The browning is not caramelisation. It is protein and sugar reacting together, and it makes hundreds of new compounds.

name: Preservation
fact: Every method does one of four things: take the water, take the oxygen, take the temperature, or take the pH.

name: Famine
fact: Rarely a shortage of food. Almost always a collapse in who can get hold of it.

name: Aqueduct
fact: Gravity does all the work, and the fall must be gentle and unbroken over tens of kilometres.

name: Sewer
fact: London built one because of the smell, and it stopped the cholera by accident.

name: Village
fact: Small enough that everyone is known, which is a form of enforcement as much as of company.

name: Farm
fact: It is an argument with succession: every field would rather be a forest.

name: Railway
fact: Steel on steel has almost no grip, which is the point and also the problem.

name: Canoe
fact: The first boats were hollowed logs, and stability came at the cost of speed from the start.

name: Raft
fact: It does not need to be watertight, which is why it is the oldest craft there is.

name: Rocket
fact: It pushes against nothing. It throws mass backwards, and the reaction is the thrust.

name: Navigation
fact: Latitude is easy and longitude is a clock problem, and that took four hundred years to accept.

name: Radioactivity
fact: Nothing you do to an atom changes when it will decay. Heat, pressure and chemistry make no difference.

name: Fusion
fact: Easy in a star and hard everywhere else, because a star has gravity holding it together and we do not.

name: Superconductivity
fact: Not very low resistance. Exactly zero, and a current started in a loop will run for years.

name: Tool
fact: Using one is common in animals. Making one to make another is nearly ours alone.

name: Pulley
fact: Each extra line halves the force and doubles the distance, and the total work is unchanged.

name: Mechanism
fact: Parts arranged so that one motion determines another, which is what makes it a mechanism rather than a heap.

name: Program
fact: Instructions stored in the same memory as the data, which is what made a computer general.

name: Network
fact: Its value rises faster than its size, which is why the second telephone was worth more than the first.

name: Artificial Intelligence
fact: The goalposts move: once something works it stops counting as intelligence.

name: Topology
fact: What survives stretching. A cup and a doughnut are the same, and the hole is why.

name: Medicine
fact: For most of its history it did more harm than good, and the turn came within living memory.

name: Drug
fact: The dose makes the poison, and there is nothing that is not a poison at some dose.

name: Dose
fact: The gap between the dose that works and the dose that harms is called the therapeutic index, and for some drugs it is very narrow.

name: Hygiene
fact: Semmelweis showed hand-washing cut deaths from 18% to 2%, and was driven out of the profession for it.

name: Vitamin
fact: Thirteen substances with nothing chemically in common. What unites them is only that we cannot make them.

name: Malnutrition
fact: It includes having too much as well as too little, and both can be in the same person.

name: Mental Illness
fact: Diagnosed almost entirely by description rather than by test, which is unusual in modern medicine.

name: Sedan
fact: Three boxes: engine, people, luggage — and the luggage box is sealed off from the cabin.

name: Hatchback
fact: Two boxes. The luggage space is inside the cabin and the back window lifts with the door.

name: SUV
fact: It began as a car body on a truck's ladder frame, which is why the early ones handled as they did.

name: Pickup
fact: An open bed behind a closed cab, and the bed is structurally separate from it.

name: Coupé
fact: Two doors, and the name comes from a cut-down horse carriage — coupé means cut.

name: Convertible
fact: Removing the roof removes most of the structure, so the floor has to be rebuilt.

name: Estate Car
fact: The roofline runs flat all the way to the tail instead of dropping.

name: Limousine
fact: Named after a region of France, for a cloak, because of the driver's hood.

name: Jeep
fact: Designed to a US Army specification in 1940 that gave the bidders 49 days.

name: Taxi
fact: Named after the taximeter, which is the actual innovation — the vehicle was already there.

name: Bulldozer
fact: The tracks matter more than the blade: they spread the weight so it does not sink into what it is pushing.

name: Fire Engine
fact: It carries a pump rather than much water. The water comes from the hydrant it parks beside.

name: Toyota
fact: It began as a loom company, and the car business was funded by selling a weaving patent.

name: Ford
fact: The moving line cut assembly of a Model T from twelve hours to ninety-three minutes.

name: Volkswagen
fact: Founded by the German state in 1937 to build one specific cheap car, and it nearly died in 1945.

name: Ferrari
fact: The road cars exist to fund the racing team, which is the opposite of every other manufacturer.

name: Tesla
fact: Named after Nikola Tesla, and the first car was a Lotus Elise with the engine taken out.

name: Mercedes
fact: Named after a customer's eleven-year-old daughter.

name: BMW
fact: It made aircraft engines first, and the roundel is the Bavarian flag rather than a propeller.

name: Honda
fact: Started by bolting surplus army generator engines onto bicycles in 1946.

name: Race
fact: The rules exist to make the comparison mean something, which is why they are always argued about.

name: Beauty
fact: Some of it is agreed across every culture ever tested, and some of it is entirely local.

name: Disorder
fact: A pattern of difficulty, named because it recurs — not because a cause is known.

name: Syndrome
fact: Symptoms that travel together, which is a clue that one thing is behind them.

name: Therapy
fact: About half the benefit across every school of it comes from things all schools share.

name: Treatment
fact: It has to be compared against doing nothing, because a great many things get better anyway.

name: Patient
fact: The word means one who suffers, and until recently it also meant one who waits.

name: Effect
fact: What follows, and separating it from what merely accompanies is most of science.

name: Cause
fact: Almost nothing has one. What is called the cause is the part that was unusual.

name: Factor
fact: One of the things a result depends on, and the interesting ones are those that limit it.

name: Variable
fact: Something that could have been otherwise, which is what makes it worth measuring.

name: Culture
fact: Growing an organism deliberately, and about 99% of bacteria will not do it.

name: Powder
fact: Grinding does not change the substance. It changes the surface, and the surface is what reacts.

name: Paste
fact: Enough liquid to move and not enough to flow, which is a narrow band.

name: Cluster
fact: Things found together more often than chance allows, which is a claim about the expected rate.

name: Group
fact: Members and a boundary, and the boundary is usually doing more work than the members.

name: Disc
fact: Spinning material flattens into one, whatever it started as, because only the spin axis survives collapse.

name: Stain
fact: Cells are nearly transparent, so almost nothing in microbiology could be seen before dyes.

name: Microscope
fact: Two lenses beat one, and the limit is not the glass but the wavelength of light.

name: Stand
fact: Something whose only job is to hold another thing still.

name: Dynasty
fact: Power inherited rather than chosen, and its problem is always the succession.

name: Sector
fact: Primary takes from nature, secondary makes, tertiary serves — and countries move through them in order.

name: Economy
fact: The study of what people do when they cannot have everything, which is always.

name: Conflict
fact: Two parties wanting things that cannot both happen, which is not the same as disliking each other.

name: Missile
fact: The difference from a rocket is that it corrects itself on the way.

name: Guidance
fact: Measure the error, act to reduce it, repeat — and almost everything that steers itself does exactly this.

name: Feedback
fact: Sending part of the output back to the input, and the sign of it decides everything.

name: Output
fact: What comes out, and what counts as it is a decision about where you drew the boundary.

name: Result
fact: What actually happened, as against what could have.

name: Molten Gold
fact: Gold melts at 1064°C and comes back exactly as it was, every time.

name: Molten Bronze
fact: It melts around 950°C — lower than either metal it is made of.

name: Travertine
fact: Freshwater limestone, laid down where groundwater loses its carbon dioxide at the surface. It is one of the few rocks you can watch being made.

name: Velebit
fact: Croatia's longest range, 145 km from Senj to the source of the Zrmanja, and karst the whole way. Its highest point is Vaganski vrh at 1,758 m.

name: Senj
fact: A harbour at the seaward end of the Vratnik pass, inhabited for more than 3,000 years because it is where the road over the Velebit reaches the Adriatic.

name: Uskoks
fact: Christian refugees from Ottoman Bosnia, resettled at Senj to hold the Habsburg frontier. Venice called them pirates; the Uskok War ended in 1617 with their expulsion.

name: Nehaj Fortress
fact: Eighteen metres tall, twenty-three wide, walls two to three metres thick, five towers and eleven cannon openings — finished in 1558 and built out of the town it was defending.

name: Plitvice Lakes
fact: Sixteen lakes in a staircase, dropping 133 m from the first to the last over barriers that are still growing by up to 13 mm a year.

name: Sticky Rice Mortar
fact: Lime mortar with boiled sticky rice in it. The starch controls how the lime crystallises, and the result outlasts lime alone by centuries.

name: Shona
fact: The people whose ancestors built Great Zimbabwe, and whose descendants were told for most of a century that they had not.

name: Lalibela
fact: Eleven churches cut downward into scoriaceous basalt — not built up but excavated out, four of them free-standing in their own trenches.

name: Great Zimbabwe
fact: Dry-stone granite with no mortar anywhere in it. The Great Enclosure wall runs about 250 m and stands 11 m high, laid course by course without a binder.

name: Olduvai Gorge
fact: Thirty miles of gorge cut 90 m down through lake beds, so the last two million years lie exposed in order. Volcanic ash from Olmoti and Kerimasi sealed each layer as it formed.

name: Obelisk of Axum
fact: Twenty-four metres and 160 tonnes of phonolite, carved as a multi-storey building with false doors and windows. Italy took it in 1937 and flew it home in three pieces in 2005.

name: Twyfelfontein
fact: More than 5,000 engravings chiselled through the dark desert varnish on sandstone, so the picture is simply the paler rock underneath.

name: Kilwa Kisiwani
fact: A Swahili city built of coral limestone that took the Sofala gold trade in the 13th century and shipped ivory, incense and cloth to Arabia, India and China.

name: Mapungubwe
fact: A kingdom of 5,000 people by 1250, trading gold and ivory for Indian glass beads. Its golden rhinoceros is gold foil over wood, and apartheid governments tried to bury the whole find.

name: Ngorongoro Crater
fact: The largest intact unflooded caldera on Earth: a volcano perhaps 5,000 m high that fell into itself two to three million years ago, leaving a 260 km² floor 610 m below the rim.

name: Desert Varnish
fact: A dark manganese and iron coating that builds on desert rock over thousands of years, thinner than a sheet of paper. Scratch through it and the pale rock beneath is your line.

name: Anangu
fact: The Pitjantjatjara and Yankunytjatjara people of the central Australian desert, to whom Uluru is sacred and who hold its title.

name: Gunditjmara
fact: The people of western Victoria who dammed a lava flow to farm eels, six and a half thousand years ago.

name: Rapa Nui
fact: The Polynesian people of Easter Island, who carved more than nine hundred moai between about 1250 and 1500.

name: Uluru
fact: A single mass of coarse arkose standing 348 m above the plain with a 9.4 km perimeter, and far more of it underground than above.

name: Budj Bim
fact: Basalt weirs, dams and channels built to hold and harvest short-finned eels. One trap at Lake Condah carbon-dates to 6,600 years — older than the pyramids and still a working idea.

name: Moai
fact: More than nine hundred figures, nearly all cut from compressed volcanic ash at one quarry, averaging 4 m and 12.5 tonnes. The largest raised weighed 86 tonnes.

name: Nan Madol
fact: Ninety-two artificial islets stacked out of natural basalt columns on a reef flat, laid like logs. Megalithic building began about 1180.

name: Sydney Opera House
fact: Its shells were unbuildable until Jørn Utzon cut every one from the surface of a single sphere, so the same precast rib could be repeated instead of individually formed.

name: Great Barrier Reef
fact: The largest structure built by living things: 2,300 km of coral, visible from orbit and made entirely of the skeletons of animals a few millimetres across.

name: Columnar Basalt
fact: Lava that cracks into hexagons as it cools and contracts, splitting downward into columns. Nature supplies the pillar already quarried.

name: Megalith
fact: A stone too big to carry, moved anyway. The whole technology is levers, rollers, ramps and a great many people who all turned up.

name: Corbel Vault
fact: Each course laid a little further in than the one below until the two sides meet. No arch, no keystone, no mortar — and Newgrange's has stood for five thousand years.

name: Skara Brae
fact: Ten stone houses on Orkney with stone beds, stone dressers and a central hearth, built where there were no trees. A storm in 1850 stripped the dune off them.

name: Newgrange
fact: A passage tomb of about 3100 BC with an opening above the door that lets the midwinter sunrise run 19 m to the back chamber for roughly seventeen minutes.

name: Lascaux
fact: Nearly 6,000 figures in iron and manganese pigment, blown through a tube or blotted on, 17,000 to 22,000 years old. Twelve hundred visitors a day damaged them in fifteen years.

name: The Iron Bridge
fact: The first cast-iron bridge, opened 1781: 30.6 m of span and 384 tonnes of iron, jointed with mortises, tenons and dovetails because the only people who knew how to join a frame were carpenters.

name: Wieliczka Salt Mine
fact: 287 km of galleries down to 327 m, worked from the 13th century to 1996, with four chapels and a chandelier carved out of the rock salt by the miners.

name: Rock Salt
fact: Halite left behind by a sea that dried up. It is soft enough to carve and strong enough to hold a roof, which is why salt mines have chapels in them.

name: Neolithic
fact: The stretch in which people started farming, staying put and building in stone. Everything monumental before metal belongs to it.

name: Abraham Darby III
fact: Third of the Coalbrookdale Darbys. His grandfather worked out how to smelt iron with coke instead of charcoal; he spent the family fortune casting the first iron bridge.

name: Jørn Utzon
fact: Won Sydney with a drawing nobody could cost, then spent years finding the geometry that made it buildable — and resigned before it opened.

name: Nabataeans
fact: Desert traders who got rich on incense and then spent it on water: dams, conduits and cisterns that turned a canyon into a city of 20,000.

name: Göbekli Tepe
fact: Limestone enclosures raised from about 9500 BCE by people who had not yet taken up farming. Monumental building came before the crop, not after it.

name: Petra
fact: Facades cut into sandstone, reached through a natural cleft only three or four metres wide. Al-Khazneh is 24 m across and 37 m high, carved top-down out of the cliff.

name: Borobudur
fact: Nine stacked platforms of andesite — six square, three round — carrying 2,672 relief panels and 504 Buddhas. Seen from above it is a mandala; walked, it is a path.

name: Nazca Lines
fact: Over 1,300 km of line made by lifting rust-coated pebbles off pale subsoil. A hummingbird 93 m long, a condor 134 m, all still there because it never rains.

name: Geoglyph
fact: A drawing made by moving what is already on the ground. Nothing is added, so the picture lasts exactly as long as the ground does.

name: Stupa
fact: A solid dome over a relic, with no interior to enter. You do not go in; you walk around it, and the walking is the point.

name: Hunter-Gatherer
fact: How everyone lived for the first ninety-five per cent of the species. Göbekli Tepe is the evidence that they built monuments too.

name: Great Mosque of Djenné
fact: The largest mud-brick building in the world, replastered every year by the whole town. The palm sticks bristling out of its walls are the scaffolding, left permanently in place.

name: Toron
fact: Bundles of palm stick left projecting about 60 cm from a mud wall. They are decoration and permanent scaffolding at once — the building comes with the means of its own repair.

name: Citadelle Laferrière
fact: Built 900 m up a Haitian mountain after independence, with 365 cannon and stores for 5,000 men for a year, against a French invasion that never came. It cost up to 20,000 lives to build.

name: Registan
fact: Three madrasahs round a square in Samarkand. One has tigers with the sun on their backs in its tilework — living creatures, in a tradition that mostly refuses them.

name: Madrasah
fact: A college built round a courtyard: lecture rooms, a mosque and cells to sleep in, all facing inward. Ulugh Beg taught astronomy in his.

name: Tilework
fact: Glazed ceramic cut and set into pattern. It survives sun and frost that would strip paint, which is why the great buildings of Central Asia are still the colour they were built.

name: Mason
fact: The trade that turns a heap of stone into a wall that stands. In Djenné the masons' guild is hereditary, and the mosque is replastered under its direction every year.

name: Guild
fact: A trade that controls who may practise it, what it costs, and who teaches the next lot. It is how a skill survives longer than the people who have it.

name: Turf
fact: Soil held together by living grass roots, cut in blocks. Where there are no trees and no stone it is the wall, the roof and the insulation at once.

name: Kuk Swamp
fact: Drainage ditches dug about 9,000 years ago in the New Guinea highlands to farm taro, and bananas by 6,900. Agriculture was invented here independently, on its own schedule.

name: Great Bath
fact: Twelve metres by seven and 2.4 deep, lined with bitumen to hold water. The oldest public water tank anyone has found, and nobody can say what it was for.

name: Cahokia
fact: A city of up to 15,000 on the Mississippi around 1100, with about 120 earthworks. Monks Mound is 30 m high and holds 622,000 cubic metres of earth, carried basket by basket.

name: Earthwork
fact: A structure made by moving soil. It needs no material anyone has to make, and no tool but a basket — which is why the largest pre-industrial structures in the Americas are earth.

name: Talud-Tablero
fact: A sloping face with a framed rectangular panel sitting on it. Teotihuacan's signature, and the way archaeologists trace its influence across Mesoamerica.

name: Farmer
fact: The first job that meant staying in one place, and the one nearly everybody did for ten thousand years.

name: Flying Buttress
fact: A half-arch standing outside the wall, catching the vault's outward push and carrying it to the ground. The wall stops holding the roof up, so the wall can be glass.

name: Gothic
fact: Pointed arch, rib vault and flying buttress, working together. Each one alone is a detail; the three at once let a stone building be mostly window.

name: Cathedral
fact: Not a size but a job: the church that holds a bishop's chair. Most take a century or more, so the people who start one are not the people who finish it.

name: Chartres Cathedral
fact: Rebuilt after the 1194 fire in about twenty-five years, which was extraordinary, and it still has 167 windows of its original glass — most cathedrals lost theirs.

name: Mont-Saint-Michel
fact: A granite outcrop 92 m high in a bay with a 14 m tidal range, so it is an island twice a day. A causeway built in 1879 stopped the scouring and silted the bay up; a dam and a new bridge undid it.

name: Mbanza Kongo
fact: Capital of the Kingdom of Kongo from about 1390 to 1915, on a mountain at a junction of trade routes. Around 1620 the city and its hinterland held some 130,000 people.

name: Monk
fact: Someone who has given up ordinary life for a rule. Monasteries kept literacy, brewing, herbal medicine and bookkeeping going through centuries when nobody else was doing them at scale.

name: Emperor
fact: A ruler of rulers. Diocletian is the only Roman one who retired, and he built somewhere to retire to first.

name: Amphitheatre
fact: A theatre doubled — seats all the way round instead of a half-circle. The word means exactly that, and the shape exists because the show is in the middle rather than at one end.

name: Diocletian's Palace
fact: A retirement palace of Brač limestone finished about 305. When Salona was destroyed its refugees moved inside the walls and never left — about 3,000 people still live in it.

name: Walls of Dubrovnik
fact: 1,940 m of uninterrupted circuit up to 25 m high, six metres thick on the landward side and as little as 1.5 on the sea. Three round towers, fourteen square, and more than 120 cannon.

name: Pula Arena
fact: The only Roman amphitheatre with its entire outer wall still standing — 132.5 m by 105.1, four storeys, and four towers each holding two cisterns.

name: Lager Yeast
fact: A hybrid of brewing yeast and a cold-tolerant wild species from Patagonia. It works below 10 °C and settles to the bottom, which is the whole difference between an ale and a lager.

name: Dextrin
fact: Starch broken into shorter chains by dry heat. It is why toasted flour thickens less than raw flour and tastes of something.

name: Silage
fact: Green fodder pickled in its own lactic acid under an airtight cover. It keeps a summer's grass edible through a winter.

name: Dried Chilli
fact: Drying concentrates the capsaicin and lets Maillard reactions run slowly, which is why a dried chilli tastes of raisin and tobacco and a fresh one does not.

name: Crystallised Honey
fact: Honey is supersaturated glucose, so it wants to crystallise. Set honey is not spoiled honey; it is honey doing what the chemistry says it should.

name: Pagoda
fact: A stupa redrawn in timber, storey by storey. The floors are not tied to the central pillar, so in an earthquake they slide against each other instead of snapping.

name: Hōryū-ji
fact: The oldest wooden buildings standing anywhere. Ring-counting puts the felling of the pagoda's central pillar at 594, which is a date read off the timber itself rather than off a document.

name: Giant's Causeway
fact: About 40,000 basalt columns, mostly six-sided, the tallest around 12 m. They are cooling cracks — the same pattern dried mud makes, propagated downward through a lava flow.

name: Stonehenge
fact: Sarsen uprights with lintels held on by mortise and tenon, cut in stone — carpentry joints in rock, by people with no metal.

name: Hadrian's Wall
fact: 117 km across Britain, built from AD 122 by three legions in about six years. A milecastle every Roman mile and a turret every third of one, so nothing crossed unseen.

name: Dendrochronology
fact: Tree rings vary with the weather, and the pattern is the same across a region. Match a beam's rings to a master sequence and you get the year the tree was felled, not an estimate.

name: Rock Alcove
fact: Where a band of shale sits inside sandstone, water seeps along it and undercuts the cliff. The overhang is not a cave — it is a seep line that ate its way in.

name: Ancestral Puebloan
fact: Farmers of the Colorado Plateau who built in stone under cliff overhangs, and left after a drought that ran from 1276 to 1299.

name: Mesa Verde
fact: Six hundred cliff dwellings of hard sandstone laid in adobe mortar, tucked under seep-cut overhangs. Occupied for seven centuries and empty by about 1285.

name: Teutonic Order
fact: A crusading order that ended up running a state on the Baltic. It built in brick because the north German plain has no building stone at all.

name: Malbork Castle
fact: The largest brick complex in Europe, 21 hectares inside its outer walls, built over 132 years. More than half of it was destroyed in 1945 and it has been under restoration since 1962.

name: Palace
fact: Where power lives rather than where it defends itself. The distinction matters: a palace is built to be seen into, a fortress to be kept out of.

name: Cenote
fact: A sinkhole into the water table. The Yucatán has no rivers at all — the limestone drains everything underground — so a cenote is the only water there is.

name: Chichén Itzá
fact: El Castillo has 91 steps on each of four faces and one at the top: 365. Around the equinoxes the northwest corner throws triangular shadows down the north balustrade that read as a serpent.

name: Inselberg
fact: An island mountain: the hard plug of an old volcano left standing when everything softer around it eroded away. Uluru and Sigiriya are both this.

name: Sigiriya
fact: A palace on a granite plug 180 m high, built 477–495 CE, entered through a gateway shaped as a lion. Its polished plaster mirror wall carries over 1,500 verses left by visitors from the 8th century on.

name: Dome
fact: An arch spun about its own axis, so every line through it is an arch. It carries itself in compression and needs no beam, which is why it can span what nothing else can.

name: Pendentive
fact: A curved triangle that lets a round dome sit on a square room. Without it a dome needs a round wall under it, and rooms are not round.

name: Hagia Sophia
fact: Built in five years and ten months, from February 532. Its first dome came down in 558; the replacement is ribbed, 33 m across and raised 6.25 m higher, and it has stood ever since.

name: Sacsayhuamán
fact: Limestone blocks of up to 200 tonnes fitted so closely a sheet of paper will not go between them, with no mortar anywhere. The largest came about 35 km.

name: Wrought Iron
fact: Iron with almost no carbon and a grain of slag stringers running through it. It bends rather than snapping, and it rusts slowly, which is why Victorian ironwork is still standing.

name: Eiffel Tower
fact: 7,300 tonnes of puddled iron in 18,038 parts, held by 2.5 million rivets. The curve of the legs is not decoration: it is the shape that balances wind load at every height.

name: Maze
fact: A plan whose purpose is to cost you time. At Himeji the keep is 130 m from the gate and the path to it is 325.

name: Himeji Castle
fact: Eighty-three buildings, white with fire-resistant lime plaster over every timber surface. Himeji was firebombed in 1945 and the castle came through; one bomb landed on the top floor and did not go off.

name: Pont du Gard
fact: 48.8 m high and 274 m long, laid dry — no mortar, no clamps, 50,400 tonnes of limestone held by friction and its own weight. It falls 2.5 cm across its whole span.

name: Surveying
fact: Measuring the ground accurately enough to build across it. A Roman aqueduct falling one metre in three thousand is a survey error budget, not a construction one.

name: Potala Palace
fact: Stone walls three metres thick and five at the base, battered inward, with copper poured into the foundations against earthquakes. The shell went up in three years and the inside took forty-five.

name: Benin Moat
fact: A ditch and rampart around Benin City, about 12 km long, reaching 17 m from the bottom of the ditch to the top of the bank. The inner Iya dates to about 1460.

name: Merv
fact: Not one city but several walled cities side by side, each built fresh on empty ground by a different era. By 1150 it may have been the largest city in the world.

name: Grog
fact: Fired clay ground up and mixed back into raw clay. It has already shrunk as far as it will, so the pot shrinks less and cracks less as it dries.

name: Conchoidal Flake
fact: Struck from glassy stone, a flake comes off in a shell-shaped curve with an edge a few molecules thick. Nothing manufactured was sharper until the twentieth century.

name: Silica Sand
fact: Quartz ground down and nothing else. Quartz has no cleavage planes, so it wears round instead of splitting — which is why the world's beaches are quartz and not feldspar.

name: Crushed Ice
fact: The same ice with far more surface. It chills a drink faster and dilutes it faster, and you cannot have one without the other.

name: Tower Karst
fact: Limestone dissolved away until only steep isolated towers are left, typically six times taller than they are wide. It needs heavy rain and warmth, which is why it is a tropical landform.

name: Hạ Long Bay
fact: Some 1,600 limestone towers standing in the sea, 20 million years in the making. The sea then cut notches at its own level into every one of them, at the same height.

name: Reservoir
fact: Water held against a dry season. Whoever controls one controls the year, which is why they are so often built where the temple is.

name: Tikal
fact: A city with no river, no lake and no cenote — it ran entirely on rainwater held in plastered reservoirs. Temple IV stands 70 m from the plaza floor to the top of its roof comb.

name: Bagan
fact: More than 10,000 temples, pagodas and monasteries raised on one plain in two centuries. About 2,200 survive; the 1975 earthquake took many and 2016 damaged nearly 400 more.

name: Shicra
fact: A loose reed bag of rubble, stacked to build a platform. It flexes in an earthquake instead of cracking, and because each bag is woven from a dated plant it tells you exactly when the wall went up.

name: Caral
fact: The oldest urban centre in the Americas, occupied from about 2600 BC. No pottery, no battlements, no weapons and no mutilated bodies — a city built before either of those things.

name: Concentric Castle
fact: A ring of wall inside a ring of wall, the inner one taller, so both can shoot at once and taking the outer gains you a killing ground rather than the castle.

name: Krak des Chevaliers
fact: Held 2,000 men and was never stormed. Baibars took it in 1271 with a forged letter from the Grand Master telling the garrison to surrender, after 36 days.

name: Balance
fact: It compares two masses rather than measuring one, so it gives the same answer on a mountain, at sea level or on the Moon. A spring scale does not.

name: Quenching Trough
fact: The water beside the anvil. Dropping hot steel into it freezes the crystal structure mid-change, which is what makes it hard — and brittle until it is tempered.

name: Drying
fact: Taking water out slowly enough that what is left does not warp. It is the longest step in papermaking, in timber, in brick and in pasta, and the one that is always rushed.

name: Pietra Dura
fact: Stone cut to a drawn shape and set flush into stone, so the picture is level with the surface and has no paint in it. It cannot fade, because nothing about it is a pigment.

name: Taj Mahal
fact: Its four minarets lean very slightly outward, so that if one ever falls it falls away from the tomb. Twenty-eight kinds of stone are inlaid into the marble, from Afghanistan, Tibet, Sri Lanka and China.

name: Suspension Bridge
fact: The deck hangs from a cable, so the span carries itself in tension. Nothing underneath has to hold it up, which is why it can cross what a pier cannot stand in.

name: Caisson
fact: An upturned box pumped full of compressed air so men can dig underwater inside it. Coming up too fast dissolves nitrogen out of the blood as bubbles, which is how decompression sickness got its other name.

name: Great House
fact: A Chacoan great house is hundreds of rooms in one planned structure, four storeys in places, and mostly not lived in. Nobody is sure what they were for.

name: Chaco Canyon
fact: Roads up to 97 km long, nine metres wide and dead straight regardless of terrain, in a culture with no wheel and no draught animal. 200,000 conifers were carried in on foot from up to 110 km away.

name: Brooklyn Bridge
fact: Its designer died of tetanus before it began and his son was paralysed by caisson disease building it, so Emily Warren Roebling ran the site for eleven years.

name: Log Building
fact: Horizontal logs notched at the corners so their own weight locks them. It needs an axe and nothing else — no saw, no nail, no mortar — which is why it is the northern forest's building method everywhere at once.

name: Shingle
fact: A thin split board laid overlapping. Split rather than sawn, so the grain runs unbroken end to end and water follows it off instead of soaking in.

name: Kizhi Pogost
fact: Twenty-two domes, 37 m high, of notched pine logs and not one nail in the structure — but about 180,000 of them holding its 60,000 aspen shingles. The famous claim is half true, and the half that is false is the roof.

name: Onion Dome
fact: Wider than the drum it sits on and drawn to a point. It sheds snow, which a hemisphere does not, and the timber frame under the sheathing carries no load from above.

name: Saint Basil's Cathedral
fact: Nine chapels on one foundation, eight around a central one. It was gilded when built; the colours came in between the 1680s and 1848, so nobody in the sixteenth century ever saw it as it looks now.

name: Brimstone Hill Fortress
fact: Designed by British engineers and built and maintained by enslaved Africans, on a hill 972 feet above the sea. Guns went up in 1689; by 1736 it carried 49 of them.

name: Sterkfontein
fact: Mrs Ples, found in 1947, dates to between 2.05 and 2.01 million years. Little Foot's date has moved from about 2.6 to about 3.4 million, which rearranges who descended from whom.

name: Patina
fact: The green skin on old copper is a mixture of copper carbonates and sulfates, and it is airtight. Unlike rust it stops the corrosion it came from, which is why a copper roof lasts centuries.

name: Linseed Oil
fact: It does not dry by evaporating — it takes oxygen out of the air and cross-links into a solid film. That reaction gives off heat, which is why a pile of oily rags can set itself alight.

name: Lachrymatory Factor
fact: Cutting an onion releases an enzyme that builds a small sulfur compound in the air. It reaches your eye, meets water, and turns into sulfuric acid, which is the whole reason you cry.

name: Verdigris
fact: Copper acetate: the green pigment made by leaving copper in vinegar fumes. It was the brightest green available for a thousand years and it eats through the paper it is painted on.

name: Galleon
fact: Built to carry cargo across an ocean and fight at the end of it. Spain sailed them in convoy because one ship alone was a prize and forty together were a problem.

name: Old Havana
fact: Founded 1519 on a bay deep enough to hold a treasure fleet. A French corsair burned it in 1555, and the first fortress went up three years later.

name: Fynbos
fact: A fire-dependent shrubland on soil so poor almost nothing else grows. Table Mountain and the Back Table hold about 1,500 plant species in 57 km² — as many as the whole United Kingdom.

name: Table Mountain
fact: Flat on top because it is the floor of an old valley: a syncline of quartzitic sandstone, 450 to 510 million years old, left standing when everything softer around it went.

name: Prison
fact: Holding people as the punishment itself, rather than while they wait for one, is a fairly recent idea. Before it, a gaol was mostly somewhere to keep you until the sentence happened.

name: Apartheid
fact: South Africa's system of racial separation in law, from 1948 to the early 1990s. It was not custom or prejudice alone but statute — registration, pass laws and separate areas, written down and enforced.

name: Robben Island
fact: A prison from the late seventeenth century until 1996. Nelson Mandela was held there for 18 of his 27 years, and it became a World Heritage Site three years after it closed.

name: Muqarnas
fact: Tiers of small niches stacked into a vault, each one holding the next. It carries almost nothing — the structure is behind it — so the ceiling reads as a honeycomb hanging in the air.

name: Alhambra
fact: Begun 1238 under the first Nasrid sultan and finished as a palace-city once a canal brought mountain water up onto the plateau. It was surrendered in 1492 without being attacked.

name: Rock-Cut Architecture
fact: Building by removing. There is no foundation, no joint and no possibility of correction — a column is whatever was left standing when the cutting stopped.

name: Ajanta Caves
fact: Thirty cave monuments cut into a basalt cliff, holding the largest surviving body of ancient Indian wall painting. A British officer out hunting tigers was shown the entrance to one in 1819.

name: Leptis Magna
fact: A Punic port that became Rome's third largest in the Mediterranean, because an emperor was born there. Abandoned, it was buried by dunes — which is why so much of it is still standing.

name: Ember
fact: Charcoal burning without a flame, because the volatiles have already gone. It glows rather than flickers, and it is hotter than the fire it came from.

name: Forced Draught
fact: Air pushed into a fire rather than drawn in. It is the whole difference between a fire that cooks and a fire that smelts — above about 1,200 °C nothing happens without it.

name: Mogao Caves
fact: Nearly 500 painted cave temples above a desert oasis, with 46,000 m² of wall painting. One of them was walled up early in the 11th century with some 50,000 manuscripts inside and not opened again until 1900.

name: Mount Fuji
fact: Four volcanoes stacked on the same spot, the newest about 10,000 years old. It has not erupted since 1707 and is not extinct — only quiet.

name: Rolled Oats
fact: Steamed and pressed flat between rollers. Flattening breaks the cell walls, which is why rolled oats cook in minutes and whole groats take an hour.

name: Nattō
fact: Soybeans fermented by a hay bacillus that lives on rice straw. It makes long threads of polyglutamic acid, which is the stringiness, and enough vitamin K2 to interfere with warfarin.

name: Firn
fact: Snow that has survived a summer and been packed by the snow above it. Halfway to ice: the crystals have fused but air still gets through, and one more year of burial closes it.

name: Rock Candy
fact: Sugar coming out of a supersaturated syrup onto a string, one molecule at a time in the same orientation. It is a crystal you can grow on a kitchen shelf and eat.

name: Clotted Cream
fact: Cream held just below simmering for hours until the fat rises and sets into a crust. Nothing is added and nothing ferments — it is only heat, time and patience.

name: Phonolite
fact: Fine-grained alkaline lava, too poor in silica to make quartz. Thin slabs ring when struck, which is where the name comes from.

name: Meroë Pyramids
fact: Steep, narrow and small: 6 to 30 m tall and raked to about 70°, where an Egyptian pyramid of the same height sat on a footprint five times larger.

name: Çatalhöyük
fact: A town with no streets. Houses packed wall to wall were entered through the roof, so the rooftops were the streets and a ladder was the front door.

name: Aqueduct of Segovia
fact: 167 arches of unmortared granite, 28.5 m at the tallest point. Nothing holds it up but its own weight.

name: Banaue Rice Terraces
fact: Rice cut into a mountainside 1,500 m up, walled with stone and rammed earth and watered by canals from the rainforest above.

name: Ziggurat of Ur
fact: A solid mass of mud brick, faced in burnt brick set in bitumen. The core is what it is made of; the facing is why any of it is still there.

name: Scale (animal)
fact: A reptile scale is not a separate plate. It is a fold of the skin with a thickened keratin layer on top, which is why a snake sheds the whole covering in one piece.

name: Wing Scale
fact: A modified bristle, flattened to a blade on a stalk. Lepidoptera means scale-wing, and the scales are the order.

name: Set (mathematics)
fact: A collection considered as one object. "Any collection you can describe" turned out to be a contradiction, so which collections exist is now settled by axiom.

name: Wave (physics)
fact: Energy moves; the medium does not. A cork on the sea goes up and down while the wave goes past it.

name: Osteoderm
fact: Bone that grows inside the skin instead of from the skeleton. Crocodile scutes, an armadillo’s shell and a Stegosaurus’s plates are the same trick, arrived at separately.

name: Cone (solid)
fact: A surface ruled by straight lines, which is why it can be rolled from a flat sheet and a sphere cannot.

name: Walls of Benin
fact: Not a wall but a ditch with its own spoil banked behind it — and not one line but thousands, dividing a whole landscape into enclosures.

name: Tiwanaku
fact: A city on the altiplano beside Lake Titicaca, whose largest single stone block weighs an estimated 131 tonnes.

name: Longmen Grottoes
fact: 2,345 caves cut into limestone cliffs over six centuries. The statues run from 25 mm to 17 m.

name: Ellora Caves
fact: The Kailasa temple was cut downward out of one rock: 85,000 m³ removed, and nothing added.

name: Prambanan
fact: Interlocking andesite blocks, no mortar. It fell in a 16th-century earthquake and was put back together stone by original stone.

name: Jelling Stones
fact: The larger one carries the first written use of the name Denmark by a Dane — a king announcing a country and a religion in the same sentence.

name: American Bison
fact: Tens of millions of them made the prairie, grazing hard and moving on before the grass was killed. Shot down to a few hundred by 1889.

name: Taputapuātea Marae
fact: The marae other maraes were founded from — a new one was consecrated with a stone carried from here, so the link across the Pacific was a physical object.

name: Latte Stone
fact: A pillar and a hemispherical cap, set in parallel rows: the foundation of a raised house, and the only megalithic tradition in the Marianas.

name: Castillo San Felipe del Morro
fact: Two and a half centuries of building on one headland, ending with walls up to 12 m thick standing 43 m above the Atlantic.

name: Head-Smashed-In Buffalo Jump
fact: Twelve metres of bone below an eleven-metre cliff. The structure is not the cliff — it is the drive lanes, hundreds of cairns long, that got the herd there.

name: Gur-e-Amir
fact: Timur’s tomb, under a ribbed azure dome 15 m across. Opened in June 1941, two days before the German invasion.

name: Lopé-Okanda
fact: Over 1,600 petroglyphs on the edge between rainforest and savanna, cut about the time iron-working reached the valley.

name: Chief Roi Mata's Domain
