fact: A grave found in 1967 by taking the oral tradition seriously enough to dig where it said, and finding a chief with more than 25 of his retinue around him.

name: Zollverein
fact: A colliery built to be looked at: cubic reinforced concrete and steel trusses, and a winding tower that became the symbol of German heavy industry.

name: Konark Sun Temple
fact: A temple built as the sun god’s chariot, with 24 carved stone wheels and seven horses. The tower over the sanctum fell in 1837.

name: Białowieża Forest
fact: Almost half the wood in it is dead — ten times a managed forest — and half of its 12,000 species need the rotting logs.

name: Amsterdam Canal Ring
fact: Three concentric canals dug in one plan in the 17th century, and the city has been the shape of that plan ever since.

name: Lock (canal)
fact: A boat lift with no machinery. Shut both gates, let water in or out, and the boat rides up or down on it.

name: Panama Canal
fact: Not a cut through the isthmus but a staircase over it: ships are lifted 26 m to a lake and let down the other side.

name: Great Stupa at Sanchi
fact: A brick dome over relics, later doubled in size and cased in stone. The gateways came two centuries after the building.

name: Kalyan Minaret
fact: Fired brick in gypsum mortar, 45.6 m of it, standing since 1127. Genghis Khan had it spared while the city around it came down.

name: Cité de Carcassonne
fact: Two concentric walls and 52 towers — and a 19th-century restoration that roofed it in slate from a region with no slate in it.

name: Rila Monastery
fact: Burned to the ground in 1833 and rebuilt by public subscription — striped arcades, 300 chambers, and frescoes finished in 1846.

name: Sungbo's Eredo
fact: More than 160 km of ditch and bank in laterite, ringing a kingdom, with 20 m from ditch floor to bank rim.

name: Volcanic Ash
fact: Not smoke — rock. Magma torn into fragments under 2 mm across, which is why it settles as a blanket and stays where it lands.

name: Joya de Cerén
fact: A Maya farming village under ten metres of ash, with the crops still in the ground and nobody in the houses. They had time to leave.

name: Monte Albán
fact: A mountain top flattened by hand, 400 m above the valley and 500 years before Christ, then built on for a millennium.

name: Fasil Ghebbi
fact: Brown basalt trimmed in wine-coloured tuff — Portuguese, Indian and Arab building put together by Ethiopian emperors behind one wall.

name: Bikini Atoll
fact: Twenty-three devices, about 77 megatons, and a fleet on the lagoon floor. Listed by UNESCO for exactly that.

name: Levuka
fact: Fiji’s first colonial capital, kept as it was because the hills behind it left no room to grow and the government left instead.

name: Sangha Trinational
fact: One forest, three countries, and the clearings in it — the bais — are where the elephants can be counted at all.

name: Pantheon
fact: Still the largest unreinforced concrete dome in the world, nineteen centuries on. It gets lighter as it goes up, on purpose.

name: Parthenon
fact: Almost nothing in it is straight. The floor bulges 10.3 cm over 70 m and the columns lean inward, so that it looks straight.

name: Knossos
fact: Lit from above rather than from the sides, so rooms deep inside a dense building still get daylight and air.

name: Meteora
fact: Twenty-four monasteries on top of conglomerate pillars, reached for three centuries only by rope, basket and removable ladder.

name: Pompeii
fact: The bodies rotted and left holes. Fiorelli poured plaster into the holes, and got the people back.

name: Mount Etna
fact: Its own height is not a fixed number: 3,403 m in September 2024, and it changes with every summit eruption.

name: Dome of the Rock
fact: An octagon built around one rock, finished in 691–2. The dome is wooden, and the one standing now replaced the original after it fell in 1015.

name: Masada
fact: A desert plateau made habitable by cisterns holding 40,000 m³ — and taken in the end by a ramp 114 m high.

name: Cappadocia
fact: Soft volcanic rock under a hard cap: the cap protects a column while everything around it goes, and then people cut houses into what is left.

name: Grand Canyon
fact: 446 km long and over 1,850 m deep, cut in about five million years through rock two billion years old.

name: Salar de Uyuni
fact: 10,582 km² of salt whose elevation varies by less than a metre — flat enough that satellites are calibrated against it.

name: Urnes Stave Church
fact: Standing on staves rather than sills, from about 1132 — and carved on the north portal in the last Viking animal style.

name: Harappa
fact: 23,500 people in flat-roofed brick houses on a near-orthogonal plan, with drains. Then the Lahore–Multan railway used it for ballast.

name: Hoover Dam
fact: Poured in blocks with 937 km of pipe inside them, because left to itself the concrete would have taken 125 years to cool.

name: Grand Canal
fact: 1,776 km of canal with a summit 42 m up, and the pound lock — invented for it in 984 — is what let boats get over the top.

name: Suomenlinna
fact: A star fort bent onto six rocky islands, called the Gibraltar of the North, surrendered after two months.

name: Tōdai-ji
fact: 500 tonnes of bronze inside what was, until 1998, the largest wooden building in the world — and the hall is 30% smaller than the one before it.

name: Qhapaq Ñan
fact: About 40,000 km of road with no wheel on it anywhere, and fibre bridges that had to be rebuilt every two years.

name: Cologne Cathedral
fact: Begun 1248, abandoned around 1560, finished in 1880 to the medieval drawings that had survived the gap — 632 years, and it was the tallest building on Earth for four of them.

name: Notre-Dame de Paris
fact: The weight of the roof is carried outside the building, which is what lets the walls be thin and the windows large. The roof itself burned in 2019.

name: Yellowstone
fact: The first national park, and the reason it is worth protecting is a magma chamber: at least 1,283 geysers and 10,000 hydrothermal features over one caldera.

name: Iguazu Falls
fact: Three layers of basalt make a two-step staircase 2.7 km wide, and about half the river goes down one throat in it.

name: Angel Falls
fact: A plunge of 807 m off the edge of a table mountain — far enough that in the dry season the water is mist before it lands.

name: Seokguram
fact: An artificial granite dome assembled with stone rivets and no mortar, which let it breathe — until a concrete restoration stopped it.

name: Port Arthur
fact: A prison whose outer wall is the sea. The only way off the peninsula was a 30-metre neck, fenced, and lined with dogs.

name: Kakadu Rock Art
fact: More than 5,000 recorded sites, some paintings up to 20,000 years old, on ground occupied continuously for around 60,000.

name: Tash Rabat
fact: Thirty-one domed stone rooms at 3,200 m, each lit through a hole at the top of its own dome.

name: Larabanga Mosque
fact: Eight metres square, twelve conical buttresses, and timbers laid through the walls — adobe needs help, and this is what the help looks like.

name: Volubilis
fact: Fifty-eight olive-pressing complexes in one Roman town, and its stone later went into Meknes.

name: Ayutthaya
fact: A capital on an island made by three rivers, which is a moat you do not have to dig — until a siege lasts fourteen months.

name: Baalbek
fact: The largest ancient block known is still lying in the quarry: 19.6 m long and an estimated 1,650 tonnes, never moved.

name: Aral Sea
fact: The fourth-largest lake on Earth in 1960, and a tenth of that by 2007. Nothing was done to the lake — the work was all done to the two rivers.

name: Sagrada Família
fact: Gaudí found his arches by hanging weighted strings upside down: a chain in tension, inverted, is a line in pure compression.

name: Hwaseong Fortress
fact: Built 1794–96 with pulleys and paid labour, and written up afterwards in ten volumes — including the wages.

name: Sundarbans
fact: A forest standing in salt and airless mud, breathing through roots that grow upward — and a sea wall for millions of people.

name: Cueva de las Manos
fact: Over 2,000 hands, 829 left to 31 right — because you hold the pipe in the hand you are better with and stencil the other one.

name: Palenque
fact: A city with mains water: a corbel-vaulted conduit over 100 m long, run under the main plaza to put a stream where the builders wanted it.

name: Palmyra
fact: A city that exists because of one spring in the desert, and got rich on the caravans that had to stop at it.

name: Aachen Cathedral
fact: Charlemagne’s chapel, built about 796 partly out of columns shipped from Rome and Ravenna — the empire assembled from pieces of the last one.

name: Moscow Kremlin
fact: Oak, then white limestone, then 2,235 m of brick wall put up by Italians between 1485 and 1495.

name: Mauna Kea
fact: 4,207 m above the sea and 9,330 m above its own base — and its summit sits above the inversion layer, which is why the telescopes are there.

name: Palace of Versailles
fact: 2,143 windows, 1,252 chimneys and 67 staircases: a palace built so a whole court could be watched living in one building.

name: Unfinished Obelisk
fact: Nearly 1,090 tonnes, a third larger than any obelisk ever raised — and still attached to the quarry floor, because it cracked.

name: Nok Terracotta
fact: Near life-size hollow heads, coil-built and burnished, fired under a heap of grass and twigs. The eyes are pierced, which is how they survived the firing.

name: Igbo-Ukwu Bronzes
fact: Lost-wax castings of ninth-century Nigeria, buried with more than 150,000 glass beads that came from Egypt and Mesopotamia.

name: Mount Kilimanjaro
fact: The highest free-standing mountain in the world, and its ice cover fell from 11.40 km² to under 1 between 1912 and 2011.

name: Niagara Falls
fact: The falls are moving upstream: hard caprock over soft shale, undercut until the cap breaks off. Diversion for power has slowed it to about 30 cm a year.

name: Mỹ Sơn
fact: Cham temples of fired brick with the ornament carved into the brick itself, and no organic trace of mortar between the courses.

name: Tassili n'Ajjer
fact: Fifteen thousand engravings of antelope, crocodile and cattle herds — in the middle of the Sahara, because it was not one.

name: Temple of the Oracle, Siwa
fact: Built of kershif — salt and mud — and palm logs, which is fine in a place with no rain until it rains for three days.

name: Djémila
fact: A Roman grid laid on a narrow triangular ridge at 900 m, where the ground was so tight the theatre had to go outside the walls.

name: Cape Coast Castle
fact: Swedish, then Danish, then Dutch, then English — and dungeons cut into the rock beneath the parade ground that could hold a thousand people.

name: Manhyia Palace
fact: Built by the British in 1925 to house the king they had exiled — and he would not take it until he had paid for it in full.

name: Drakensberg Rock Art
fact: Between 35,000 and 40,000 San works, the largest such collection anywhere, painted on soft sandstone under a hard basalt cap.

name: Lamu Old Town
fact: Built of the reef and the swamp — coral rag walls on mangrove poles — and still worked by about 3,000 donkeys, because the streets were never sized for anything else.

name: Dzanga-Sangha
fact: Forest elephants gather in one clearing to eat the mineral soil, which is the only reason anyone has ever been able to watch them properly.

name: Loango
fact: A coastal kingdom that exported copper and cloth to Europe before it exported people, and outlived the trade that made it famous by only a few decades.

name: Tsodilo
fact: Four quartzite hills standing out of the Kalahari with over 4,500 paintings on them, and the San call it the birthplace of all life.

name: Old Quebec
fact: The only walled city north of Mexico, in two halves — one on top of a cliff and one at the bottom of it.

name: Copán
fact: A staircase of 62 steps carrying 2,200 glyphs — the longest Maya text there is, and it is a flight of stairs.

name: Red Fort
fact: A water channel called the River of Paradise runs through the palaces, so the cooling is part of the architecture rather than added to it.

name: Anuradhapura
fact: Capital for about 1,500 years, with brick stupas among the largest structures of the ancient world and a fig tree that has been documented since it was planted.

name: Kronborg
fact: Built where the Sound is only 4 km wide, so that a king could make every ship entering the Baltic pay him.

name: Geirangerfjord
fact: A glacier cut a valley below sea level and left; the sea came in. The farms on the cliffs above were reached by paths bolted to the rock.

name: Neuschwanstein
fact: A medieval fantasy with central heating, running hot water, flushing lavatories and telephone lines — and only about fifteen rooms ever finished.

name: Dead Sea
fact: 439.78 m below sea level and 9.6 times as salty as the ocean, because water arrives and only ever leaves as vapour.

name: Erdene Zuu
fact: Built in 1585 out of the stones of Karakorum, and destroyed in 1939 by a purge that killed more than ten thousand monks.

name: Hue Citadel
fact: European bastion geometry laid out for a Vietnamese emperor, nearly 10 km round with walls 21 m thick — and 150 of its 160 buildings were destroyed in 1968.

name: Sukhothai
fact: A city built around its ponds, and the 1292 inscription found in it is where written Thai starts.

name: Prague Castle
fact: The largest ancient castle in the world, almost 70,000 m², with a cathedral inside it that took six centuries to finish.

name: Waitangi Treaty Grounds
fact: The Treaty of New Zealand was signed in a marquee on a lawn on 6 February 1840, and the country has argued about the two texts of it ever since.

name: Haʻamonga ʻa Maui
fact: Three coral limestone slabs, the uprights 30 to 40 tonnes each, raised about 1200 AD on an island with no quarry stone but reef.

name: Otrar
fact: A caravan city that killed a caravan in 1218, and the war that answered it reached the Danube. Forty families were left by 1800.

name: Patan Durbar Square
fact: Newar brick and timber with 136 courtyards and 55 major temples, in a valley that keeps knocking them down.

name: Trogir
fact: A Greek grid from the 3rd century BC, still legible under everything Rome, Venice and the Middle Ages put on top of it.

name: Euphrasian Basilica
fact: The best-preserved early Christian church there is, standing on two older ones — the floor of the 5th-century basilica is still underneath it.

name: Sighișoara
fact: Each tower in the wall belonged to a guild and was maintained by it, so the defence of the town was divided up like its trades.

name: Te Wāhipounamu
fact: 2.6 million hectares named for the greenstone in it — the best surviving sample of what Gondwana looked like.

name: Auschwitz-Birkenau
fact: 1.1 million people were murdered here, 960,000 of them Jews. It is preserved as evidence, and it has been a museum since 2 July 1947.

name: Vigeland Installation
fact: 212 sculptures by one man, including a 14.12 m column of 121 figures cut from a single block by three masons over fourteen years.

name: East Rennell
fact: The largest raised coral atoll in the world: its lagoon is now a brackish lake sitting at sea level, on land that used to be underwater.

name: Puʻuhonua o Hōnaunau
fact: A wall that made the ground inside it legally different: reach it after breaking a kapu and a priest could absolve you instead of the law killing you.

name: Morne Trois Pitons
fact: A flooded fumarole 82–92 °C at the edge and hotter in the middle, in a valley of boiling mud and small geysers.

name: Cueva de las Maravillas
fact: 472 Taíno paintings and about 10 engravings, 25 m underground in a limestone reef that used to be a reef.
